articles.title: WTA apologizes after hot mic captures Pegula’s ‘diva’ remarks about Andreeva
articles.summary: WTA admits players were not told mics were live. Pegula called Andreeva ‘diva’ who ‘needs to be humbled’ Practice livestreams to continue without audio. The WTA has apologized and admitted it did not tell players their on-court conversations during practice sessions at the WTA Finals were being…
body: A controversy has erupted in Indian Wells after Jessica Pegula was heard on the WTA’s YouTube livestream making derogatory comments about Mirra Andreeva and her coach, Conchita Martínez.

A conversation between Pegula and her coach, Mark Knowles, has been widely scrutinized, with the American criticizing the attitude of the Russian. Pegula can clearly be heard calling the 19-year-old a “diva” and saying she has lost respect for former Wimbledon champion Martínez for not calling out her behavior.

“If I was a coach and my girl, you just played four great games, and you’re up four-zero, and you’re mad at me, hitting balls at me, I would be like, first of all, [that’s] disrespectful to the other person,” Pegula said. “You’re up 4-0, shut the fuck up. But she just can’t.”

Pegula goes on to say Andreeva would be better than her fellow American Coco Gauff if she had the same mentality. Another practice session, meanwhile, saw world No 1 Elena Rybakina having an apparent spat with her coach.

articles.title: Concacaf revamps Gold Cup format to make tournament ‘more competitive’
articles.summary: Group stage to involve two groups of eight teams. Change resembles model of Uefa Champions League. Concacaf on Thursday announced changes to the format of the Gold Cup, the confederation’s regional championship.
body: Once the primary focus of teams in the region, the 35-year-old tournament will return for its 19th edition in 2027 having lost a bit of luster. The federation’s tweaks to the format – which center around the competition’s group stage – could help restore that. Here’s a look at the tournament, what’s at stake and what is changing.

The Gold Cup is the biannual regional championship for countries within Concacaf (the Confederation of North, Central American and Caribbean Association Football). Concacaf has crowned a regional champion in one way or another since the 1960s, but the confederation took strides towards standardizing the competition’s format – and more closely mirroring the championships of other global confederations – in 1991, when it introduced the Gold Cup.

The 16 participants in Gold Cup qualify via the Concacaf Nations League, a convoluted competition that awards eight berths through group-stage play and another seven via a second-chance style tournament for lower-placing teams. The remaining slot is filled by a guest country, most recently Saudi Arabia, who participated in the 2025 edition and will return next year.

articles.title: Australian F1 world champion Alan Jones dies aged 80
articles.summary: Jones one of just two Australians to win F1 title after triumph in 1980. He won 12 grands prix across 10 seasons before retirement in 1986. Alan Jones, the 1980 Formula One world champion, has died aged 80, leading to a string of tributes from across the sport.
body: Jones won 12 F1 grands prix across his career and became just the second Australian, after Sir Jack Brabham, to be crowned world champion when he claimed the title with Williams in 1980.
In a statement, Williams said: “Everyone at Williams is deeply saddened to learn of Alan Jones’ passing.

“Alan was instrumental in making Williams what it is today, forming an extraordinary bond with Frank Williams and Patrick Head to become our first Drivers’ World Champion in just our fourth season in Formula 1.
“He set the standard for Williams champions: a fast, uncompromising racer with a challenger mentality who loved motor racing and dedicated his life to it.

articles.title: 'I don't fear for my safety from online abuse - because we're so used to it'
articles.summary: Britain's Jodie Burrage speaks to BBC Sport about the online abuse she received after her recent defeat - and why it no longer comes as a surprise.
body: After struggling with her blood pressure as she lost her first WTA Tour singles match for 16 months, Jodie Burrage checked in with three things: a doctor, a physiotherapist, and her phone.
On her social media feed there were already messages promising punishment - and others making threats on her life - for losing 3-6 6-3 7-5 to Indian wildcard Vaishnavi Adkar.
"I try not to actually read what they say," Burrage told BBC Sport from Chennai, where she is still competing in the doubles.
"Because we are so used to it - which is really quite sad - I don't fear for my safety.

articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli has revealed details of his celebrations after being crowned Formula 1 world champion, along with some of the messages he received in the aftermath of his historic triumph.
body: The 20-year-old Italian finished third in Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix to become the sport's youngest-ever drivers' title winner, achieving the feat with four rounds of the 2026 season still remaining.
Despite having the final leg of a triple-header to come this weekend with the Sao Paulo Grand Prix in Brazil, a party was held on Sunday night in Mexico at which Antonelli said he did not hold back.
Asked whether Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord had been the "biggest party animal", Antonelli told Sky Sport Germany: "Bradley's good. But I was not joking either.
"I never drink. I try to avoid that as much as possible, also because I prefer eating pasta ragu from my mother.

articles.title: Northants' Lynn served drugs ban after Blast final
articles.summary: Northants batter Chris Lynn returned a positive drugs test after playing in this season's T20 Blast Finals Day, the Cricket Regulator has revealed.
body: Former Northants Steelbacks batter Chris Lynn returned a positive drugs test after playing in this season's T20 Blast Finals Day, the Cricket Regulator has announced.
Cocaine's metabolite benzoylecgonine was found in Lynn's urine sample and he was given a one-month suspension, which has now been served.
The 36-year-old top-scored with 39 runs in their semi-final win over Somerset, before making four as they beat Hampshire in the final at Edgbaston on 18 July.
Lynn admitted using cocaine, external in the week before Finals Day - during the evening of 15 July and the early hours of 16 July.

articles.title: LIV Golf scraps plans for 'LIV 2.0' and is 'winding down operations'
articles.summary: LIV Golf has confirmed it plans to wind down operations and enter the liquidation phase, instead of launching a new version, because of a lack of financial support.
body: A lawyer representing the organisation announced the decision in a bankruptcy court hearing on Thursday in New Jersey, ending months of speculation over LIV Golf's future in the men's game.

"The debtors were ultimately unable to bring the key parties to a fully consensual arrangement that would have supported a financially viable LIV 2.0 league," Gibson Dunn partner Matthew Williams, one of LIV's attorneys, said.
"As a result, the debtors are not currently proceeding with the LIV 2.0 plan. Instead, the debtors are toggling to a value-maximising wind down of their business."

The Financial Times first reported on Wednesday that BC Partners Credit, who had been lined up as potential backers following the withdrawal of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund in April, had pulled out of a deal worth more than $300m (£220m).

articles.title: NFL viewership stabilizes after early-season declines as league nears midway point
articles.summary: After some viewership declines during the early portion of the season, the NFL is back on track. Entering Week 9, NFL viewership is up 3% year-over-year, according to a report by Austin Karp in Sports Business Journal.
body: NFL telecasts are averaging 18.4 million viewers through Week 8. The two top audiences of the year both belong to the Kansas City Chiefs and CBS. Chiefs-Raiders averaged 28.45 million viewers on the network in October, and last weekend’s Chiefs-Broncos game averaged 28.18 million viewers. Fox holds the next two most-watched contests; Commanders-Cowboys in September (27.21 million viewers) and 49ers-Seahawks in October (26.70 million viewers).

Per Karp, CBS is up 5% overall through Week 8, averaging 19.6 million viewers. Thursday Night Football on Prime Video also continues to trend up, averaging 17.6 million viewers per game. Each of its seven telecasts have seen year-over-year gains. ESPN’s Monday Night Football is up 22% versus last year, though it’s unclear if that number is buoyed by last year’s doubleheaders, which depressed ESPN’s per-game average and would make for a more favorable comparison. Figures for Fox’s and NBC’s viewership through Week 8 were not published.

articles.title: Palmer to return? Mainoo recall? Tuchel's England squad dilemmas
articles.summary: Cole Palmer's form for Chelsea ought to make him a shoo-in for England’s final international squad of 2026. The question is whether Thomas Tuchel has lost patience with him.
body: Palmer was hugely disappointed when he was overlooked for the World Cup in the summer after a stop-start season due to injury, and he withdrew from the last England camp in September and October because of a minor fitness issue.

The 24-year-old has been unavailable for selection due to injury three times since Tuchel took over, and he has withdrawn from two further squads after being named. He has only played three times for his country since the German coach took the reins in January 2025.

But Palmer is one of the most in-form forwards in the Premier League right now. Eight goal involvements in 11 matches testify to that, although Morgan Rogers, who has had a hand in 10 goals, and Jude Bellingham, who's contributed to nine, have better stats.
If Palmer were left out, it would be a pointed statement from the England boss and would raise serious doubts about his international future under Tuchel.

articles.title: Arsenal star told why he should consider Bundesliga move
articles.summary: Martin Odegaard has been linked with a potential move to Bayern Munich, with the Arsenal captain being advised to consider joining the German giants if an opportunity arises. The Norwegian has established himself as one of the most important players in Mikel Arteta’s squad.
body: Arsenal have no intention of selling Odegaard or any of their key players, meaning Bayern would face a difficult task if they wanted to bring him to the Bundesliga. The midfielder also appears happy in North London, having produced several impressive performances since becoming an important part of the team.

However, reports suggest he could be open to considering a move to Bayern, one of Europe’s leading clubs. Eivind Bisgaard Sundet believes the switch would make sense for the Arsenal captain and has explained why he could benefit from the change.

Odegaard’s technical ability and creativity could make him an attractive option for Bayern, particularly given the style of football the German side plays. His ability to influence possession and create opportunities would potentially suit a team that often dominates its domestic matches.

There is also the possibility that a move to Germany could offer the midfielder a different physical and competitive schedule compared with the Premier League. Sundet believes those factors could make Bayern an appealing destination if Odegaard ever decides to leave Arsenal.
